source.title: Per-parameter Task Arithmetic for Unlearning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Cheng-Yi Cai; Ze-Sheng Ye; Jiang-Chao Yao; Jian-Zhong Qi; Bo Han; Xiaolu Zhang; Feng Liu; Junlin Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figures and tables are flattened in the web text, but Table 12's metric values are assignable; no relevant result is figure-only.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a quantization attack to its own PerTA unlearning method and reports post-attack unlearning and utility metrics, testing whether quantization restores forgotten information with a different unlearning method.
record.gate_note: Table 12 reports PerTA-grad before and after a quantization attack. The table gives averages across TOFU's 1%, 5%, and 10% unlearning tasks rather than separate task results. Other reported experiments compare unlearning methods but do not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper applies a quantization attack, the attack Version D names, to its own new unlearning method (PerTA-grad) on TOFU. It reports forget-set metrics before and after the attack in Appendix C.6, Table 12. This bears on D (does quantization restore forgotten knowledge?) and on F (does a newer method resist it?). All other experiments compare unlearning methods without any recovery attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say quantization's impact on PerTA is limited and PerTA still outperforms other methods after the attack. But the GA/GD/NPO/NPO+ rows in Table 12 are their unattacked Table 1 values, so this compares attacked PerTA with unattacked baselines.
record.recipe_differences: PerTA uses a per-parameter weighting of a task vector for unlearning, rather than the gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU procedures named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The quantization attack's effect is reported only as an average over TOFU's 1%, 5%, and 10% unlearning tasks; quantization settings are not stated.
record.problems: The quantization configuration, including bit-width, is not stated. The attack results are averaged across three unlearning tasks, with no task-specific values or uncertainty reported. The study tests only PerTA-grad on the stated attack setting.
record.rows_left_out: No other Table 12 metrics were included because they do not directly measure recovery of forget-set knowledge or retained general utility.

untested.parts: Bit-width and quantization scheme are not stated. The original unlearning methods (GA, GD, NPO, RMU) were not quantized as a control. No per-task values for the 1%, 5% and 10% splits are given, and no accuracy-based recovery measure is reported.
Robustness to relearning by fine-tuning, internal edits and prompting attacks is not tested. Quantization is tested only on the 1B model.
No attack is applied to the original methods (WMDP/RMU, WHP) or to the GA/GD/NPO baselines.

record.verdict_notes: Table 12's baseline rows are identical to Table 1, so the baselines were never quantized. There is therefore no evidence in this setup that quantization recovers knowledge for any method, which weakens the robustness claim. The record's F reason saying PerTA stays closer than the compared methods 'after attack' is misleading. The study cites Zhang et al. (ICLR 2025) on quantization recovery but does not replicate its bit-width settings.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports FQ, extraction strength, and utility rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance. Its attack test is quantization only.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack using a small set is reported.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is reported.
The paper does not state the quantization bit-width or test multiple quantization settings.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context-information attack is reported.
Robustness is evaluated for quantization only, not the fine-tuning, internal-edit, or prompting attacks.

rows.note: FQ is reported as higher-is-better. The post-attack score is lower, indicating some loss of unlearning effectiveness, but the table does not quantify recovered accuracy.
